event.description: Tie query and key projections within each attention block while retaining independent value/output projections, reversed padded operands, d=14, two heads, two blocks, ff=19, rank-3 learned positions, and the 45000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is 3129 parameters at 99.190000%, a +0.190000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the accepted starting model used tied input/output embeddings (6080, 100.00%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0020, feed-forward sharing across layers, an optimization failure with 58.95% peak validation; 3 prior parameter-tying candidate attempts. The immediately preceding rank-2 reversed-input attempt-0036 is an optimization failure (45000 steps, 11.1% peak validation, no checkpoint), not a scored nonqualification. Hypothesis: a common query/key feature map may suffice for content-similarity attention in the fixed-format task while independent value and output projections preserve information transport and head mixing; this removes one 14x14 matrix per block, reducing actual parameters from 3129 to 2737. This is a representational parameter-tying change, not scalar pruning. It is more informative than the nearest untested cross-layer-attention sharing alternative because it isolates within-layer attention-score symmetry without coupling the two sequential attention computations.
